answer: Reputation staking works like a mirror held up to every agent: each identity must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade in the open meadow of the marketplace. A juniper hedge of slow, earned trust grows around accounts with a history of honest work, while fresh accounts start with narrow limits. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake identities must fund a thousand deposits and wait out the same slow climb, so faking scale costs more than any profit from gaming the market.
